model: P&C insurer FCFE at cost of equity, net debt held at zero (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR (153%) is off the FY2022 trough (EPS $1.19 on a 95.8 CR plus $1.9bn investment losses) and is not a growth rate. Equity CAGRs understate economic compounding because PGR pays out most earnings through the annual variable dividend (FY2025 year-end equity is net of the $8.0bn December-declared dividend). Revenue 3/5yr CAGRs (20.9%/15.5%) reflect the 2023-2025 hard-market rate cycle (rate + 10% annual PIF growth) and are not projected forward; forward base growth is 3.5-6%.
historical_growth.notes: Annual CAGRs FY2020/FY2022 -> FY2025, unchanged by a quarterly filing. FCF CAGRs use reported OCF-capex, which for an insurer is dominated by float build; they are shown for completeness only and not used. SBC is ~0.15% of revenue and flat in dollars ($121M/$122M/$132M FY2023-25), so the SBC adjustment does not move any CAGR.

items.would_move_it: NPW growth below 3% or PIF growth below 4% for two consecutive quarters (toward bear), or rate decreases ending with NPW back above 7% (toward bull).

items.assumption: Through-cycle combined ratio: base ~92 (11.8% margin), bull ~90 (13.5%), bear ~94 (10.0%), and the FY2027-28 glide to it
items.why_unchanged: Q3 CR 88.7 with accident-year loss ratio +3.9pt confirms the direction of the base glide (87.5 -> ~90 -> ~92) without changing its destination; the ten-year average has not moved.
items.would_move_it: A calendar-year CR above 92 already in FY2027, or management reversing rate cuts (toward bear); accident-year loss ratio stabilising while PIF growth holds at 6%+ (toward bull).

items.why_unchanged: No new annual SBC disclosure; dilutive RSUs 1.3M shares, unchanged in scale.

items.would_move_it: A statutory rate change or an effective rate outside 20-22% for a full year.

items.why_unchanged: Debt-to-total-capital 19.6% and statutory surplus $35.6bn on ~$89bn trailing NPW (2.5:1) show no change in capital policy.
items.would_move_it: A stated change to the 3:1 premiums-to-surplus target, or rating-agency pressure on leverage.

items.why_unchanged: No change in the rate environment large enough to matter since October; caps are multi-year trading-range judgments.
Q3 was better than feared on catastrophes and worse on underlying severity; the cycle-turn argument for a symmetric weighting stands.
items.would_move_it: The FY2026 full-year CR and January-2027 variable dividend, and Q1-2027 rate filings.

scenario_narratives.base: Normalisation, not collapse: FY2026 is the last year of exceptional margins (~88 CR; nine months at 87.5, Q3 at 88.7 with accident-year severity rising), the CR reverts to PGR's ~92 ten-year average by FY2028 as the soft market and heavy advertising bite, and growth slows to 4.5-5% before re-accelerating with the next hard cycle. Most earnings are distributed (variable dividend + buybacks); ~1.1-2% of revenue is retained to fund premium growth at a 3:1 premiums-to-surplus target.
scenario_narratives.bull: PGR's telematics and segmentation edge keeps it at a ~90 CR through a shallow soft market while property and small-commercial add growth; revenue compounds ~7% for four years from FY2027 and the market keeps paying ~17x distributable earnings.
scenario_narratives.bear: Loss-cost inflation and competitor re-pricing push the CR to ~95-96 for two years (2022 echo), growth stalls at ~2%, and the through-cycle CR settles at ~94; the market re-rates PGR to ~12x.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value PGR on what it can distribute to shareholders after funding premium growth, discounted at the cost of equity. The key judgment is the through-cycle combined ratio: every 1pt of CR is ~0.95pt of pretax margin, ~$800M of after-tax earnings on FY2025 revenue and roughly $22-25/share of base value. The base case assumes PGR's ten-year average CR (~92), not the 87-88 of 2025-26 nor its 96 ceiling.
key_risks_to_valuation: Combined ratio: a 2pt miss on the through-cycle CR (92 -> 94) moves base value by ~$45/share
Soft-market growth: rate cuts plus record advertising spend could slow premium growth below 4% while compressing margin (Q3-2026 NPW already +4%)
Loss-cost inflation (parts tariffs, used-car values, medical, litigation) outrunning rate: Q3-2026 accident-year loss ratio +3.9pt YoY, partly masked by 2.4pt of favourable prior-year development
Catastrophe/weather volatility in property and auto physical damage (9M-2026 $1.4bn, 2.2pt)
Investment portfolio: NII is ~4% of revenue; falling yields would trim margin ~0.3-0.5pt; mark-to-market on a 3.4-year duration book hits book value not the flows
Capital intensity: if regulators or rating agencies push premiums-to-surplus below 3:1, retention per $ of growth rises and distributable FCFE falls

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 total revenues $87,671M less net realized/unrealized investment gains $727M (FY2025 10-K XBRL RealizedInvestmentGainsLosses). Gains are mark-to-market noise, not a compounding revenue stream. Net premiums earned $81,661M (94%), net investment income $3,549M (4%), fees/service revenues the rest. FY0 is still FY2025: the Q3-2026 10-Q updates the FY2026 year-one drivers, not the base.
inputs.share_count_basis: 579,362,175 common shares outstanding at 2026-10-01 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover) plus ~1.3M dilutive RSUs (Q3-2026 diluted 582.2M vs basic 580.9M weighted) = 580.7M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and PGR's stated policy is to repurchase shares to neutralize equity-award dilution in the year of grant; opportunistic buybacks beyond that are a use of the FCFE, not an extra value source.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY0 FCFE proxy, NOT owner FCF: FY2025 pretax income $14,223M less $727M investment gains = $13,496M (already after $132M SBC and $278M interest), taxed at 21% = $10,662M, less equity retained to back FY2025 premium growth (0.33 x $11,836M ex-gains revenue growth = $3,906M) = $6,756M distributable.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: OCF $17,548M less capex $348M (FY2025). Meaningless for an insurer: operating cash flow includes float build (unearned premium and loss reserve growth) that is invested in the portfolio and backs policyholder liabilities, not free to shareholders. 9M-2026: OCF $12,492M less capex $317M.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K: AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $132M (FY2024 $122M, FY2023 $121M); treasury shares acquired for restricted-stock tax liabilities $92M (FY2025 parent cash flow, 10-K Schedule II). The flows charge SBC expense only (0.15% of revenue); the withholding buyback is the cash settlement of the same expensed award and adding it again with a flat share count would double-count.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025: $74M open market + $92M for equity-award tax withholding. 9M-2026: $1,490M open market + $73M withholding (7.7M shares, ~$1.6bn; Q3 alone 2.25M shares at an average $209.21) under the May-2026 25M-share authorization, 20.96M shares remaining. Authorizations are not spend; only financing-line cash counted.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY 8.5%, not a WACC, because the flows are post-interest FCFE (holdco interest $278M FY2025, $87M in Q3-2026 = ~$350M run-rate after the March-2026 $1.5bn senior notes, sits inside the pretax margin). Build: 10-year UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~0.85 (PGR's observed beta is ~0.4-0.6, deliberately rounded up because P&C underwriting margins are cyclical and catastrophe-exposed). USD flows, USD rate. Same rate in all three scenarios: risk is carried in the combined-ratio paths and the probability weights, not stacked into the discount rate. UNCHANGED in this update.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: operating leases immaterial for an insurer; no lease adjustment in flows or bridge.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: Held at ZERO. Senior notes of $8,389M at 2026-09-30 (debt-to-total-capital 19.6%, policy ceiling 30%; $1.0bn matures January/March 2027 and is now classed short-term) are serviced inside the flows; deducting them again after capitalising a post-interest stream would count the debt twice. The ~$99bn investment portfolio and policyholder reserves are operating items (float), not net cash. The $5.8bn held in the non-insurance holdco subsidiary is NOT added: it includes the 2026 note proceeds, PGR treats it as catastrophe/growth capital, and 9M-2026 retained earnings that will fund the January-2027 variable dividend are already in the FY2026 flow.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity on a US P&C insurer, run through the owner-FCF component engine with net debt at zero -- the IAG.AX / GL precedent (memory: iag-insurance-australia-group, gl-globe-life). Model UNCHANGED from the 2026-10-02 build. The dcf-methods routing table default for insurers is BVPS-compounding x exit P/B; overridden because PGR does not compound book: it distributes most earnings through an annual variable dividend ($13.60/share, $8.0bn paid January 2026) so GAAP equity is a distribution-timing artefact, and AOCI swings $1-3bn with rates (9M-2026 OCI -$2.8bn). The owner-FCF DCF is wrong for the same reasons it is wrong for any insurer: OCF/capex include float. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = total revenues ex investment gains; ebitda_margin_path = pretax margin before SBC (underwriting margin on NPE + net investment income - interest - other); da_pct = 0; capex_pct_path = equity retained to back premium growth (0.33 of incremental revenue: the 3:1 premiums-to-statutory-surplus target for vehicle lines, ~80% equity-funded given the ~20% debt-to-capital policy, plus a buffer), i.e. 0.33 x g/(1+g) of revenue; cash_tax_rate = 21% (FY2025 effective 20.5%; 9M-2026 effective 21.3%). MARGIN ANCHORS: FY2025 combined ratio 87.4 -> pretax margin pre-SBC ex gains 15.7%; 9M-2026 CR 87.5 -> 15.7% (pretax $11,011M less $314M gains on $68,675M revenue ex gains, plus SBC); management target is 'grow as fast as we can at or below a 96 CR'. PGR's 10-year average CR (2016-2025) is ~92, which maps to ~11.8% pretax margin -- the base-case through-cycle anchor. Q3-2026 UPDATE (10-Q filed, now used as an anchor): companywide CR 88.7 (Q3-2025 89.5, which carried 4.6pt of one-off policyholder credit expense, so the underlying comparison is ~84.9 -> 88.7); loss/LAE ratio 68.1, +3.7pt YoY, accident-year +3.9pt on higher severity; catastrophe losses $388M = 1.8pt (Q3-2025 $219M, 1.1pt; 9M $1,429M, 2.2pt); expense ratio 20.6 with advertising $1.6bn, +18%, adding 0.8pt; favourable prior-year development 2.4pt. Q3 pretax margin pre-SBC ex gains 14.7% (H1 16.1%). Growth: Q3 NPW +4%, NPE +5%, PIF +6% (40.5M), average written premium per policy -2% personal auto on rate decreases; revenue ex gains Q3 +5.2%, 9M +6.5%. Capital: statutory surplus $35.6bn, holdco non-insurance subsidiary $5.8bn. The prior build's fear of a ~89.3 catastrophe-heavy Q3 did not materialise: the quarter was better on catastrophes and worse on underlying severity. WHAT CHANGED: FY2026 (year one) growth and margin in all three scenarios, plus the year-one retention that follows mechanically from growth. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: FY2027+ growth, the margin glide to the through-cycle CR in each scenario, SBC%, tax, retention ratio 0.33, cost of equity, terminal growth and caps, probability weights -- see unchanged_assumptions. DATA FIXES NOT MADE: PGR_Metrics.csv TotalDebt reads 0 for FY2021-FY2025 and blank for 2026 quarters but the senior notes are $6.9bn (FY2023-FY2025) and $8.4bn (Q3-2026 10-Q debt note); this needs a make-fix correction by the financial-parser, not a DCF edit.

bear.narrative: A 2022-style loss-cost shock: tariffs on parts, social inflation and severity outrun rate while competitors (GEICO, State Farm) re-price aggressively. FY2026 still lands at +5.5% and a 14.5% margin because nine months are booked (that needs a ~93 CR, ~11% margin Q4 with growth at +2.5%); PGR then restricts growth (revenue +2% FY2027-28) and the CR drifts to ~95-96 (9-10% pretax margin, the 2021-2023 average) before settling at ~94 rather than returning to 92. Terminal 2.5%, capped at 12x FCFE, the bottom of PGR's post-2010 trading range.
bear.growth_rates_note: Year one 5.0 -> 5.5: nine months at +6.5% put a floor under the year; years 2-10 unchanged.
bear.ebitda_margin_path_note: Year one 14.0 -> 14.5: with 9M at 15.7%, 14.0 required a ~96 CR fourth quarter; 14.5 still assumes a ~93 CR Q4. Years 2-10 unchanged.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue +6.0% (9M revenue ex gains +6.5%, Q3 +5.2%, Q3 NPW +4%; Q4 assumed ~+4.5%) with a ~88 CR year: nine months booked at 87.5 and a Q4 assumed at ~89.5-90 as accident-year severity (+3.9pt in Q3) and rate decreases earn in, giving a 15.2% pretax margin. The 2027-2028 soft turn: PGR has been cutting rates and spending heavily on advertising (+18%) to grow, so premium growth slows to 4.5-5% and the CR mean-reverts to its ~92 ten-year average (11.8% pretax margin) by FY2028 and holds there. Growth re-accelerates to 6% as the cycle hardens again and property/Commercial (Coterie BOP/GL) add volume, then glides to 3.5%. Equity retained to back growth at 0.33x incremental revenue. Terminal at min(Gordon 8.5%/3.0%, 15x FCFE).
base.growth_rates_note: Year one 6.5 -> 6.0 on the Q3-2026 10-Q; years 2-10 unchanged.
base.ebitda_margin_path_note: Year one 15.0 -> 15.2: Q3 pretax margin 14.7% beat the ~13.9% H2 the prior path implied; years 2-10 unchanged.

bull.narrative: Telematics/pricing edge keeps compounding share: FY2026 closes at +6.3% (Q4 ~+5.5%) with a Q4 margin near 15%, then PIF growth stays high single digit as property and Commercial Lines add a second and third engine, revenue +7% through FY2029. The soft market is shallow and PGR's segmentation lets it hold a ~90 CR (13.5% pretax margin) through the cycle, roughly its 2018-2020 and 2024-2025 average. Terminal 3.5% growth (PGR keeps taking ~1pt of share a decade in a ~4% nominal market), capped at 17x FCFE, in line with its 10-year average trading multiple.
bull.growth_rates_note: Year one 7.0 -> 6.3: with nine months booked at +6.5% and Q3 NPW +4%, a 7% year would need Q4 +8%, which the filing does not support; years 2-10 unchanged.
bull.ebitda_margin_path_note: Unchanged, including year one (15.5 needs a Q4 pretax margin of ~15%, in line with Q4-2025's 15.2%).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default, UNCHANGED from the prior build: FY2025-9M 2026 margins (87-88 CR) are at a cyclical high, and the Q3-2026 10-Q shows the turn in progress (CR 88.7, accident-year loss ratio +3.9pt on severity, personal auto average premium -2% on rate cuts, advertising +18%, NPW growth down to +4%). With the P&C pricing cycle turning, downside to the through-cycle margin is as likely as upside, so bull is not over-weighted. Solvency risk is negligible (debt-to-capital 19.6%, statutory surplus $35.6bn), so bear is a margin case, not a capital case.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
